name: Binary owner or descriptor API drift
failureClass: NoClassDefFoundError, NoSuchMethodError, NoSuchFieldError or verifier failure after a dependency update
trigger: A dependent mod references a class/member owner or descriptor that the installed dependency replaced while preserving equivalent behavior.
repair: Prove old and new symbols from exact bytecode/source, then patch or recompile only the dependent references. Preserve all unrelated JAR entries and dependency semantics.
verification: Entry-level diff limited to intended classes
Old symbol absent and new symbol present
confidence: high when both API sides and behavior are proven

name: Data namespace or schema defect
failureClass: Registry bootstrap, codec, jigsaw, recipe, loot, tag, NBT or data-pack load failure
trigger: Packaged data points to a missing namespace/key/schema while sibling resources and target registries prove the intended replacement.
repair: Patch only the proven resource/NBT fields, preserve every other entry and produce a semantic diff in addition to a byte diff.
confidence: high when sibling data and registry evidence agree

name: Mixin annotation and retention contract
failureClass: InvalidMixinException claiming @Mixin or an injection annotation is absent or malformed
trigger: A locally stubbed or shaded annotation has the wrong retention, target, descriptor, package or visible/invisible annotation table placement.
repair: Compile against the real Mixin API where possible; otherwise reproduce every annotation contract exactly and rebuild affected mixin classes.
verification: Compare against real Mixin annotation retention/targets
confidence: high when classfile annotation placement is directly verified

name: Separate compatibility adapter
failureClass: Two correct mods duplicate, conflict or omit a cross-mod integration path
trigger: The smallest robust fix can observe both APIs and suppress/translate only the overlapping behavior without modifying either upstream JAR.
repair: Build a separate version-gated compatibility mod with narrow hooks, explicit config, diagnostics and fail-closed behavior.
confidence: medium to high depending on runtime coverage

name: Repair supersession and failed-attempt memory
failureClass: A statically plausible repair fails in the user's exact runtime or is replaced by a stronger repair
trigger: Fresh evidence disproves an earlier completion claim or identifies a deeper root cause.
repair: Mark the old record superseded, preserve its failure evidence, link the new artifact/record and retest the original reproducer plus regressions.

name: Declared compatibility is not binary compatibility
failureClass: Mod metadata accepts a dependency/version range but runtime linkage or mixin application fails
trigger: Actual class/member use, descriptors, injection targets or behavior changed inside a permissive declared range.
repair: Trust exact bytecode/API usage and target runtime evidence over permissive metadata; update, patch or adapt the dependent mod.
verification: Expected symbol proven in dependent bytecode
